3] In brief, the facts of the case are that on the basis of a written complaint filed by the prosecutrix on 27.06.2023, the FIR has been lodged against the present petitioner wherein it is alleged that the petitioner has committed rape on the prosecutrix continuously since 22.12.2018 till 10.06.2023 i.e.,
for a period of around five and half years.
It is alleged in the FIR that the petitioner and the prosecutrix are the resident of Village - Khawasa, Tehsil - Thandla, District Jhabua and are known to each other since long.
The prosecutrix's case is that she was proposed by the petitioner in the year 2018.

However, she refused the proposal and thereafter, he again proposed her for around 3 to 4 times to which she informed the petitioner that since he is already married, she does not want to talk to him, to which the petitioner informed her that he would take divorce from his wife and then marry her.

It is her further case that around five years ago, on 22.12.2018, the petitioner called her at his house at around 1'O clock in the noon, after threatening that she would kill her parents if she does not come, and when she reached there, she was raped by the petitioner on the threat that he would kill her mother and father and subsequently, on many occasions he has committed rape on her.

She has also stated in the FIR that she also got married on 05.03.2023, but thereafter also the petitioner used to call her and used to pressurize her that she should also call him back, and subsequently he also pressurized her to take divorce from her husband.

It is also stated that on 10.06.2023, when she was at her parents' house, he came to her house and again committed rape on her, and on 14.06.2023, when she again come to her parents' house, he again threatened her.

Thus,
after she informed her parents about the incident, the FIR has been lodged on 27.06.2023.

4] Counsel for the petitioner has submitted that based on the aforesaid FIR, the charge-sheet has already been filed and the matter is pending before the trial Court, however, on a perusal of the FIR itself, it is apparent that no case under Section 376 of IPC can be made out against the petitioner as the prosecutrix was a consenting party all along and she has never opposed or made any complaint to any person, including the police.

5] Counsel has also drawn the attention of this Court to certain photographs of the prosecutrix's marriage in which the petitioner was also present, and it is also submitted that from the photographs it is apparent that the prosecutrix and the petitioner were enjoying a good relationship and there appears to be no element of threat posed by the petitioner in any manner.

It is submitted that no reason has been assigned as to why the FIR has not been lodged earlier and apart from the bare oral allegations, there is nothing on record to suggest that the petitioner ever threatened the prosecutrix.
6] Shri Piyush Shrivastava, learned counsel for the petitioner has also drawn the attention of this Court to the various WhatsApp chats between the petitioner and the prosecutrix to submit that both of them were having a normal relationship, and various messages have also been sent by the prosecutrix herself which also demonstrate that she never felt threatened in the company of the petitioner or to have chat with him.

It is also submitted that on the alleged date of incident i.e.,
22.12.2018, the petitioner was not in town as he was attending the meeting of his employer company at Indore.

An affidavit of his senior is also filed in support of his alibi, along with a certificate of Jayesh Rawat vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 16 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45555164/
2 appreciation, which was given to him by the company on 22.12.2018.

District Jhabua on 23.06.2023 (Annexure A/14) against the prosecutrix.

8] In support of his submission and that it was a consensual relationship and does not amount to rape; counsel has relied upon the decisions rendered by the Supreme Court in the case of Pramod Suryabhan Pawar vs. State of Maharashtra and another reported as (2019) 3 SCC (Cri.) 903; Dr.

sentences.text: ] Counsel for the respondent/objector, on the other hand, has opposed the prayer.
An objection to the petition has also been filed, although not denying the factum of the photographs of the petitioner with the prosecutrix and also the WhatsApp chats.
It is submitted that the documents are the matter of evidence and cannot be relied upon at this stage by this Court.
It is also submitted that the prosecutrix was minor at the time when she was raped by this petitioner as she has stated that the earliest incident to be of 2018.
It is also submitted that the evidence is yet to commence, and the petitioner would have ample opportunity to cross-examine the prosecutrix on all these points.

Thus,
it is submitted that the petition be dismissed.
10] Counsel for the State has also opposed the prayer and it is submitted that no case for interference is made out.
11] Heard counsel for the parties and perused the record.

12] On perusal of the record, it is found that the FIR in the present case was lodged on 27.06.2023 at 16.13 hours,
under Section 376 and other Sections including he POCSO Act, in respect of the incident which took place between 22.10.2018 and 10.06.2023, i.e., after around five years and half month from the initial date of incident.

It is fond that so far as the delay is concerned, the prosecutrix has stated that she got afraid and, hence, did not tell the incident to her parents, but after she informed them about the incident, she lodged the report on that day only.
However, she has not stated as to what were the change circumstances which led her to lodge the FIR.

13] It is also found that the petitioner has filed various photographs of the prosecutrix's marriage in which he has also participated with his wife and daughter, and from a bare perusal of the photographs, which have not been rebutted by the prosecutrix in her reply/objection, it is apparent that both of them were enjoying a good relationship.

14] Petitioner has also filed various WhatsApp chats between him and the complainant of the months of January, February and March, 2023, whereas, the FIR was lodged on 27.06.2023, and these chats also it is apparent that there was normal conversation between the petitioner and the complainant, and the element of force on the part of the petitioner is clearly missing from the aforesaid chats 15] Although, the prosecutrix/complainant is represented by the counsel in this Jayesh Rawat vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 16 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45555164/
3 petition, however, no rebuttal has been filed in respect of the photographs and the WhatsApp chats,
and in fact, in the entire objection, there is not even a reference of the aforesaid photographs and the WhatsApp chats, which the petitioner has filed, which also gives rise to a presumption of innocence in favour of the petitioner 16]

sentences.text: It is also found that even according to the prosecutrix, the petitioner was having sexual relationship with her every now and then since 22.12.2018, and it is also not her case that he forced her not to marry any other person, in fact what she has stated is that the petitioner asked her to marry to some other person and subsequently asked her to give divorce to him and that he would also give divorce to his wife.

This conversation, which the prosecutrix has stated to have taken place between them, clearly indicates towards the fact that the complainant was a consenting party, and it is not a case of petitioner entering into physical relationship with the prosecutrix on some threat.

17] So far as the documents relied upon by the petitioner are concerned, this Court can rely fruitfully upon the decision rendered by the Supreme Court in the case of Rukmini Narvekar Vs. Vijaya Satardekar and Others reported as (2008) 14 SCC 1.

sentences.text:
The relevant para of the same reads as under:
"38.

In my view, therefore, there is no scope for the accused to produce any evidence in support of the submissions made on his behalf at the stage of framing of charge and only such material as are indicated in Section 227 Cr.P.C. can be taken into consideration by the learned magistrate at that stage.

However, in a proceeding taken therefrom under Section 482 Cr.P.C. the Court is free to consider material that may be produced on behalf of the accused to arrive at a decision whether the charge as framed could be maintained.

This, in my view, appears to be the intention of the legislature in wording Sections 227 and 228 the way in which they have been worded and as explained in Debendra Nath Padhi's case (supra) by the larger Bench to which the very same question had been referred."

(Emphasis Supplied) 18] Regarding the consensual sex, the Supreme Court, in the case of Deepak Gulati v. State of Haryana reported as (2013) 7 SCC 675, has held as under:-
"21.

entities.text: Deepak Gulati v. State of Haryana reported as (2013) 7 SCC 675
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Consent may be express or implied, coerced or misguided, obtained willingly or through deceit.
Consent is an act of reason, accompanied by deliberation, the mind weighing, as in a balance, the good and evil on each side.

There is a clear distinction between rape and consensual sex and in a case like this, the court must very carefully examine whether the accused had actually wanted to marry the victim, or had mala fide motives, and had made a false promise to this effect only to satisfy his lust, as the latter falls within the ambit of cheating or deception.
There is a distinction between the mere breach of a promise, and not fulfilling a false promise.

Thus, the court must examine whether there was made, at an early stage a false promise of marriage by the accused; and whether the consent involved was given after wholly understanding the nature and consequences of sexual indulgence.

There may be a case where the prosecutrix agrees to have sexual intercourse on account of her love and passion for the accused, and not solely on account of misrepresentation made to her by the accused, or where an accused on account of circumstances which he could not have Jayesh Rawat vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 16 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45555164/
4 foreseen, or which were beyond his control, was unable to marry her, despite having every intention to do so.

entities.text: Jayesh Rawat vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Such cases must be treated differently.
An accused can be convicted for rape only if the court reaches a conclusion that the intention of the accused was mala fide, and that he had clandestine motives.
xxxxxxx 24.

Hence, it is evident that there must be adequate evidence to show that at the relevant time i.e. at the initial stage itself, the accused had no intention whatsoever,
of keeping his promise to marry the victim.

There may, of course, be circumstances,
when a person having the best of intentions is unable to marry the victim owing to various unavoidable circumstances.
The "failure to keep a promise made with respect to a future uncertain date, due to reasons that are not very clear from the evidence available, does not always amount to misconception of fact.
In order to come within the meaning of the term "misconception of fact", the fact must have an immediate relevance".

Section 90 IPC cannot be called into aid in such a situation, to pardon the act of a girl in entirety, and fasten criminal liability on the other, unless the court is assured of the fact that from the very beginning, the accused had never really intended to marry her."
(Emphasis supplied) 19] This judgment has also been followed by Supreme Court in subsequent judgments i.e., in the cases of Pramod Suryabhan Pawar (supra) and Dr. Dhruvaram Murlidhar Sonar (supra).
20] In such facts and circumstances of the case, when the FIR is lodged after a delay of five and half years, and the prosecutrix also knew that the petitioner was already married and the fact that she also got married to which the petitioner never objected, this Court does not find it to be a case of rape and it is apparent that the prosecutrix was a consenting party all along.
21]

In view of the same, the petition stands allowed and the FIR lodged at Crime No.467 of 2023 under Sections 366, 376, 376(2)(n) & 506 of IPC and Section 5/6 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 as also against the proceedings pending before the Special Judge, Jhabua in Special Sessions Trial No.58 of 2023
